failure.title: article to product SPA navigation, back, forward and repeated opt-ins leave no ad contexts

initialDefaultOffAttempt.explanation: The cold dev server returned the SPA Home navigation in approximately 5.5 seconds, exceeding the original 5 second URL expectation. Only URL expectations changed to the existing public-route 30 second tolerance; iframe cleanup, repeated-instance and sandbox assertions were not relaxed. The complete default-off rerun passed.

failure.title: consent alone does not load ads and explicit opt-in remains blocked by the app CSP

initialEnabledAttempt.explanation: Chrome redacted static data URLs to empty blockedURI in DOM violation events and blockedURL in native CSP audits. An expectation for literal data therefore failed despite browser error documents. A diagnostic audit probe also failed that exact URL expectation. A subsequent frame-owner probe passed: native frameNavigated.unreachableUrl equals the static helper URL and DOM.getFrameOwner associates that frameId with the exact banner/native iframe src. The final complete rerun requires those exact owned failures together with fresh parent enforce/frame-src originalPolicy equal to the response header and matching native non-report-only frame-src issues. Network safety interception cannot satisfy these checks, and the data document never reached its safety interceptor. Unknown supplier behavior remains unverified.

failure.title: publishes one canonical article with metadata, factual boundaries and an official source

targetedOffColdSeoBudget.explanation: Four targeted default-off cases passed. The multi-resource SEO test exhausted its 30 second test budget during cold /sitemap.xml compilation, after its article metadata/fact/source assertions. Its whole-test budget is now 60 seconds; individual assertions are retained. The parent requested stopping old-base browser work for integration with main 41c0855726012efbd4054a7e1fac95c4ea5caed9, so this latest budget adjustment awaits its post-integration rerun. The same SEO test passed in complete default-off and final enabled runs.

limitations: Application response CSP was never replaced or relaxed. No advertising domain was added to script-src or frame-src.

External request interception is a safety guard and is not proof of CSP rejection. Fresh DOM enforce/frame-src events matching the response policy, native non-report-only frame-src issues and exact frameId/owner/src/unreachableUrl association establish the active static document rejection separately. Chrome redacts blockedURI/blockedURL, so those individual fields cannot identify the URL.
Resource timing entries cannot establish network transfer success or completeness. Request events from opaque frames can be incomplete.

Standalone canaries certify static data transport, browser sandbox restrictions and context destruction for harmless inline code. They do not certify real supplier creative behavior or actual native format responsiveness.

The publisher domain may be exposed as ancestorOrigins in Chromium. No claim of hiding the public site origin is made; private article path, query, referrer and account data are excluded from the static document transport.
A local database template has no running backend; public catalog reads can log connection errors. Tests perform no account, checkout, image generation, payment, email or advertising click action.
